post_process/trim/queue_new_entry), MutatorRegistry with dynamic weights, GrammarMutator,
CmpLog/RedQueen mutator, MOpt PSO-based mutation scheduling (pilot/core phases with velocity/position
updates), and PowerScheduleEnsemble rotation.

with seed=42.

slug: afl
title: "AFL: Coverage-guided Greybox Fuzzing"
description: |
  Implement the core AFL (American Fuzzy Lop) fuzzing algorithm with full paper-faithful
  mechanisms including: 64KB shared memory bitmap with hit count bucketing (1,2,3,4-7,8-15,
  16-31,32-127,128+), edge coverage tracking via (prev_block XOR cur_block)>>1, fork server
  simulation, test case calibration (multi-run stability detection), input trimming (powers-of-two
  block removal preserving coverage), corpus culling via greedy set cover (smallest+fastest per edge),
  full deterministic stages (walking bitflip 1/2/4, byte flip 8/16/32, arithmetic add/sub 1-35 for
  8/16/32 bit widths with both endianness, interesting values 8/16/32, auto-dictionary extraction
  during bitflip, user+auto dictionary insertion), havoc stage (random stacked mutations 2^1-2^7
  operations), splice stage (midpoint combination of two seeds followed by havoc), performance
  scoring based on exec speed/coverage/depth/stability, crash deduplication via coverage hash,
  and queue scheduling with favored seed priority (75/25 split).
depends_on: []
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/afl_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh

  - coverage-guided fuzzing
  - 64KB edge coverage bitmap
  - hit count bucketing (classify_counts)
  - fork server model
  - test case calibration (stability detection)
  - input trimming (powers-of-two)
  - corpus culling (greedy set cover)
  - power schedule (constant energy)
  - deterministic mutation stages (bitflip 1/2/4/8/16/32, arithmetic, interesting values, dictionary)
  - auto-dictionary extraction during bitflip
  - havoc stage (random stacked mutations)
  - splice stage (combining test cases)
  - crash deduplication via coverage hash
  - performance scoring (exec speed, coverage, depth)
  - queue scheduling (favored seed priority)

  AFL_PATHS_DISCOVERED: 10
  AFL_UNIQUE_CRASHES: 1
  AFL_CORPUS_SIZE: 10
  AFL_EDGE_COVERAGE: 86.7
===== requirements/aflfast.yaml =====
slug: aflfast
title: "AFLFast: Power Schedules via Markov Chain Model"
description: |
  Implement AFLFast's power schedules based on modeling fuzzing as a Markov chain.
  Each unique execution path is a state; mutations cause transitions between states.
  The key insight is that AFL's constant energy wastes effort on high-frequency paths.
  AFLFast assigns energy inversely proportional to path frequency f(i) and exponentially
  in selection count s(i). Includes: EXPLOIT schedule (p(i)=alpha, same as AFL),
  EXPLORE schedule (p(i)=alpha/beta, normalized), COE schedule (cut-off exponential:
  skip seeds with f(i)>mu, otherwise min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i), M)), FAST schedule
  (recommended: min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i) / f(i), M)), LINEAR schedule (min(alpha/beta *
  s(i)/f(i), M)), QUAD schedule (min(alpha/beta * s(i)^2/f(i), M)). Also implements
  PathFrequencyTracker (Markov state identification, transition counting, rare path
  detection), seed prioritization strategies (prioritize_small_s for FAST/COE,
  prioritize_small_f for explore/linear/quad), EnergyComputer with Gini coefficient
  analysis, and schedule comparison utilities.
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflfast_schedules.py
  - fuzzsim/aflfast_search.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflfast_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - Markov chain path model
  - path frequency tracking (f(i) = inputs exercising path i)
  - selection count tracking (s(i) = times seed i was chosen)
  - power schedule variants (FAST, COE, explore, exploit, linear, quad)
  - energy assignment formulas (exponential, linear, quadratic)
  - cut-off mechanism (skip over-fuzzed seeds)
  - upper bound M on energy (prevent explosion)
  - seed prioritization by s(i) and f(i)
  - Markov state transitions and probability estimation
  - rare path identification and bonus
  - energy distribution analysis (Gini coefficient)
expected_outputs:
  AFLFAST_PATHS_FAST: 10
  AFLFAST_PATHS_COE: 10
  AFLFAST_SPEEDUP: 1.00
  AFLFAST_MEAN_ENERGY: 198.5
===== requirements/aflgo.yaml =====
slug: aflgo
title: "AFLGo: Directed Greybox Fuzzing"
description: |
  Implement AFLGo's directed greybox fuzzing with distance-based seed prioritization
  and simulated annealing for exploration-to-exploitation transition. Two-level distance
  computation: (1) Function-level via BFS on reverse call graph from target functions,
  (2) Basic-block level combining CFG shortest paths with function distances via harmonic
  mean. CallGraph class with function/edge management. CFGDistance class with BFS-based
  shortest path computation. Distance normalization to [0,1] range. Seed distance via
  minimum block distance among covered edges. Simulated annealing with exponential cooling
  schedule T(t)=T0*alpha^(t/t_x*K), plus alternative cooling schedules (linear: T0*(1-t/t_x),
  logarithmic: T0/(1+log(1+t/t_x*K)), adaptive: adjusts alpha based on progress). Energy
  assignment formula: p(s,T)=base*((1-d(s))*(1-T)+0.5*T) transitioning from uniform (T=1)
  to distance-proportional (T=0). Seed skipping during exploitation phase (T<0.3, d>0.9).
  DistanceComputer class orchestrating the full pipeline. Phase detection (exploration/
  transition/exploitation).
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflgo_distance.py
  - fuzzsim/aflgo_annealing.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflgo_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - directed greybox fuzzing
  - call graph construction and BFS traversal
  - CFG shortest path computation
  - function-level distance via reverse BFS
  - basic-block level distance via harmonic mean
  - distance normalization to [0,1]
  - seed distance aggregation (minimum, harmonic mean)
  - simulated annealing (exponential cooling)
  - alternative cooling schedules (linear, logarithmic, adaptive)
  - exploration vs exploitation phases
  - temperature-based energy assignment
  - seed skipping during exploitation
  - time-to-exposure (TTE) metric
expected_outputs:
  AFLGO_DISTANCE_ACCURACY: 100.0
  AFLGO_DIRECTED_TTE: 939
  AFLGO_UNDIRECTED_TTE: 1103
  AFLGO_SPEEDUP: 1.17
===== requirements/aflpp.yaml =====
slug: aflpp
title: "AFL++: Modular Fuzzing Framework"
description: |
  Implement AFL++'s modular framework with full custom mutator API and MOpt PSO-based
  mutation scheduling. Custom Mutator API matching AFL++ afl-fuzz-mutator.c: init(),
  fuzz(buf, add_buf), fuzz_count(buf), havoc_mutation(buf, max_size),
  havoc_mutation_probability(), post_process(buf), trim(buf), describe(),
  queue_new_entry(buf, coverage). MutatorRegistry: register/unregister mutators,
  weighted random selection, dynamic weight adjustment (1.1x on success, 0.99x on
  failure, min 0.1). Built-in mutators: GrammarMutator (token templates, structured
  input generation, grammar-aware trimming), CmpLogMutator (RedQueen comparison
  operand recording and substitution for bypassing magic bytes). MOpt PSO scheduler:
  pilot phase (independent operator testing, L iterations each), core phase (PSO
  velocity update: v=w*v+c1*r1*(pbest-x)+c2*r2*(gbest-x), position update: x=x+v,
  velocity clamping [-0.3, 0.3], probability bounds [0.02, 0.50], normalization to
  valid distribution). Operator set: bit_flip, byte_flip, arith_add, arith_sub,
  interesting, random_byte, havoc_1, havoc_2. Personal/global best tracking, fitness
  history, convergence monitoring. PowerScheduleEnsemble: rotate through FAST/COE/
  EXPLORE/QUAD/LIN schedules per queue cycle.
depends_on:
  - afl

  - fuzzsim/aflpp_custom_mutator.py
  - fuzzsim/aflpp_mopt.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflpp_experiment.py

  - run.sh

  - mutator registry with dynamic weighted selection
  - grammar-based mutation (token templates)
  - CmpLog/RedQueen (comparison operand replacement)
  - Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for operator selection
  - PSO velocity/position update equations
  - pilot phase (independent operator testing)
  - core phase (continuous PSO optimization)
  - inertia weight, cognitive/social components
  - velocity clamping and probability bounds
  - personal best and global best tracking
  - operator success rate monitoring
  - dynamic probability adjustment
  - PowerScheduleEnsemble (schedule rotation)

  AFLPP_CUSTOM_MUTATOR_PATHS: 10

"""Edge coverage bitmap (64KB shared memory simulation)."""

from typing import Set


MAP_SIZE = 65536  # 64KB bitmap


class CoverageBitmap:
    """Simulates AFL's coverage bitmap using a set of edge IDs.

    In real AFL, this is a 64KB shared memory region where each byte
    represents a hit count for an edge (hashed to bucket). We simplify
    to exact edge tracking for determinism.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.global_coverage: Set[int] = set()
        self.virgin_bits: Set[int] = set()  # edges never seen before

    def has_new_bits(self, edges: Set[int]) -> bool:
        """Check if the given edges contain any new coverage.

        Returns True if at least one edge has never been seen before.
        """
        new_edges = edges - self.global_coverage
        return len(new_edges) > 0

    def update(self, edges: Set[int]) -> Set[int]:
        """Update the global bitmap with new edges.

        Returns the set of newly discovered edges.
        """
        new_edges = edges - self.global_coverage
        self.global_coverage.update(edges)
        self.virgin_bits.update(new_edges)
        return new_edges

    def get_coverage_count(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of unique edges covered so far."""
        return len(self.global_coverage)

    def get_coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
        """Return coverage as a percentage of total edges."""
        if total_edges == 0:
            return 0.0
        return len(self.global_coverage) / total_edges * 100.0

    def reset(self):
        """Reset the bitmap to empty state."""
        self.global_coverage.clear()
        self.virgin_bits.clear()

"""TestCase dataclass for fuzzing seeds/corpus entries."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Set


@dataclass
class TestCase:
    """Represents a test case (seed) in the fuzzing queue."""

    data: bytes
    coverage: Set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
    exec_time: float = 0.0
    is_crash: bool = False
    depth: int = 0
    fuzz_count: int = 0  # how many times this seed has been fuzzed
    was_fuzzed: bool = False
    is_favored: bool = False
    times_chosen: int = 0  # number of times selected for fuzzing
    creation_time: int = 0  # iteration when this was added to queue
    unique_edges: Set[int] = field(default_factory=set)  # edges only this TC covers

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(id(self))

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return self is other

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        """Return the size of the test case data in bytes."""
        return len(self.data)

    def copy(self) -> 'TestCase':
        """Create a shallow copy of this test case."""
        return TestCase(
            data=self.data,
            coverage=set(self.coverage),
            exec_time=self.exec_time,
            is_crash=self.is_crash,
            depth=self.depth,
            fuzz_count=self.fuzz_count,
            was_fuzzed=self.was_fuzzed,
            is_favored=self.is_favored,
            times_chosen=self.times_chosen,
            creation_time=self.creation_time,
            unique_edges=set(self.unique_edges),
        )

Properties:
- 50 basic blocks, 80 edges

- Rich set of rare edges

from fuzzsim.program_model import SimulatedProgram, BasicBlock, Edge
from typing import Tuple, Set, Dict
import numpy as np


def build_binutils_sim() -> SimulatedProgram:
    """Build a binutils-like simulated program with 50 blocks and 80 edges."""
    blocks = [BasicBlock(i) for i in range(50)]

    edges = []
    edge_id = 0

    # Layer 0: entry (block 0) branches to 4 handlers
    for dst in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 0, dst))
        edge_id += 1

    # Layer 1: each handler branches to 2-3 sub-handlers
    # Block 1 -> 5, 6, 7
    for dst in [5, 6, 7]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 1, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 2 -> 8, 9
    for dst in [8, 9]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 2, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 3 -> 10, 11, 12
    for dst in [10, 11, 12]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 3, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 4 -> 13, 14
    for dst in [13, 14]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 4, dst))
        edge_id += 1

    # Layer 2: deeper processing blocks
    # Block 5 -> 15, 16
    for dst in [15, 16]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 5, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 6 -> 17, 18
    for dst in [17, 18]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 6, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 7 -> 19, 20
    for dst in [19, 20]:
        is_rare = (dst == 20)
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 7, dst, is_rare=is_rare))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 8 -> 21, 22
    for dst in [21, 22]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 8, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 9 -> 23, 24
    for dst in [23, 24]:
        is_rare = (dst == 24)
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 9, dst, is_rare=is_rare))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 10 -> 25, 26
    for dst in [25, 26]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 10, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 11 -> 27, 28
    for dst in [27, 28]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 11, dst, is_rare=(dst == 28)))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 12 -> 29, 30
    for dst in [29, 30]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 12, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 13 -> 31, 32
    for dst in [31, 32]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 13, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    # Block 14 -> 33, 34
    for dst in [33, 34]:
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 14, dst, is_rare=(dst == 34)))
        edge_id += 1

    # Layer 3: converge to processing blocks
    # Blocks 15-34 -> blocks 35-44
    for src in range(15, 25):
        dst = 35 + (src - 15) // 2
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, src, dst))
        edge_id += 1
    for src in range(25, 35):
        dst = 40 + (src - 25) // 2
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, src, dst))
        edge_id += 1

    # Layer 4: final blocks -> exit blocks
    # Blocks 35-44 -> blocks 45-49
    for src in range(35, 45):
        dst = 45 + (src - 35) // 2
        is_crash = (src in [38, 43])  # crash paths
        is_rare = (src in [37, 42])
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, src, dst, is_crash=is_crash, is_rare=is_rare))
        edge_id += 1

    # Back edges for loops
    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 35, 5, is_rare=True))
    edge_id += 1
    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 40, 10))
    edge_id += 1
    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 42, 12))
    edge_id += 1

    # Additional cross-edges
    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 16, 21))
    edge_id += 1
    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 22, 30))
    edge_id += 1
    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 28, 33, is_rare=True))
    edge_id += 1

    # Pad to 80 edges with additional paths
    while edge_id < 80:
        src = 45 + (edge_id % 5)
        dst = 49
        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, src, dst))
        edge_id += 1

    target_blocks = [38, 43, 49]
    return SimulatedProgram(blocks, edges, entry_block=0,
                            target_blocks=target_blocks)


class BinutilsSimProgram:
    """Wrapper with binutils-sim specific execution logic."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.program = build_binutils_sim()
        self.total_edges = len(self.program.edges)

    def execute(self, input_data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
        """Execute binutils_sim with input-dependent path selection."""
        edges_hit = set()
        is_crash = False
        exec_time = 0.002

        if len(input_data) < 2:
            return edges_hit, False, exec_time

        # Use first bytes to navigate through layers
        b0 = input_data[0] if len(input_data) > 0 else 0
        b1 = input_data[1] if len(input_data) > 1 else 0
        b2 = input_data[2] if len(input_data) > 2 else 0
        b3 = input_data[3] if len(input_data) > 3 else 0
        b4 = input_data[4] if len(input_data) > 4 else 0

        # Layer 0: select handler
        handler = b0 % 4
        edges_hit.add(handler)  # edge 0-3

        # Layer 1: sub-handler selection
        if handler == 0:
            sub = b1 % 3
            edges_hit.add(4 + sub)  # edges 4-6
            current = 5 + sub
        elif handler == 1:
            sub = b1 % 2
            edges_hit.add(7 + sub)  # edges 7-8
            current = 8 + sub
        elif handler == 2:
            sub = b1 % 3
            edges_hit.add(9 + sub)  # edges 9-11
            current = 10 + sub
        else:
            sub = b1 % 2
            edges_hit.add(12 + sub)  # edges 12-13
            current = 13 + sub

        exec_time += 0.001

        # Layer 2: deeper processing
        layer2_base = 14
        block_offset = current - 5
        if block_offset >= 0 and block_offset < 10:
            edge_in_layer2 = layer2_base + block_offset * 2 + (b2 % 2)
            if edge_in_layer2 < len(self.program.edges):
                edges_hit.add(edge_in_layer2)

        exec_time += 0.001

        # Layer 3: convergence
        layer3_start = 34
        convergence_edge = layer3_start + min(b3 % 10, 9)
        if convergence_edge < len(self.program.edges):
            edges_hit.add(convergence_edge)

        # Layer 4: final
        layer4_start = 54
        final_edge = layer4_start + min(b4 % 10, 9)
        if final_edge < len(self.program.edges):

            edges_hit.add(final_edge)
            if edge.is_crash:

        exec_time += 0.001 * len(edges_hit)
        return edges_hit, is_crash, exec_time

    def get_total_edges(self) -> int:

    def get_crash_edges(self) -> Set[int]:

    def get_rare_edges(self) -> Set[int]:
